stages.sub: After this stage the student can draw and analyse the labour market diagram, apply shifts, and explain why elasticity and maximum wages matter.

steps.q: New machinery lets each worker produce far more output, so firms want to hire more workers at every wage rate. Which curve moves, and which way?
steps.right: The demand for labour curve shifts right
steps.wrong: The supply of labour curve shifts right
steps.hint: It is firms' wish to hire that changed, not workers' willingness to work.

steps.q: Demand for nurses barely falls even when their wages rise a lot, because hospitals still need enough staff. Demand for fruit-pickers falls sharply when their wages rise, since farms can use machines instead. If wages rise by the same amount in both markets, in which market will employment fall by more?
steps.right: The fruit-picker market, since demand responds more there
steps.wrong: The nurse market, since wages matter most there
steps.hint: Which demand curve is more sensitive to a wage change: the flat responsive one or the steep unresponsive one?

steps.right: No, jobs lost will differ because responsiveness differs
steps.wrong: Yes, the same wage rise means the same job losses
